desc: Derive the structural characterization of connectivity in the disjoint-interval graph, including an efficient method to identify connected components.
Derive and prove a bounded-hop canonical-path theorem for vertex-weighted shortest paths.
Find a shortest-path formulation that leverages interval ordering and avoids constructing the potentially quadratic graph.
Design preprocessing data structures for minimum-weight vertices satisfying left/right endpoint constraints.
Prove the shortest-path reduction is correct, including endpoint-cost accounting.
Develop an implementation-ready algorithm with complexity analysis under \(N,Q \le 2\times10^5\).
Check edge cases including isolated vertices, direct adjacency, duplicate/nested intervals, and disconnected components.
